Third test build of Ionium, Celeritas running on Minecraft 1.8.9 Forge. Still a pre-release, so expect bugs and keep a backup of your worlds.

**Setup is the same as pre.1.** It needs Java 21, RetroFuturaBootstrap (we use [8to25](https://github.com/Oondanomala/8to25)) and LWJGL 3 from the launcher, plus ION Client for the LWJGL 2 compatibility layer. If something is missing, Ionium shows a dialog at launch that tells you what.

This build is about everything that is not terrain. Terrain was already well ahead of OptiFine in our benchmarks; the places where OptiFine still won were text, item frames and signs, which vanilla 1.8.9 draws in slow ways.

Performance:
- Text is drawn in one batch per line instead of one GL call block per character. That is every nametag, hologram, scoreboard, chat line, sign and the F3 screen. A lobby with 80 players, holograms and a scoreboard went from about 375 to 405 fps; a platform with 827 signs from 224 to 433 fps. OptiFine does 502 there, but it skips the sign text at that distance, Ionium still draws it.
- Compasses in item frames no longer rewrite the block atlas twice per item frame per frame. A platform with 250 mobs and 240 item frames went from 220 to 257 fps (OptiFine: 230).
- Sign text is wrapped and measured once per sign instead of every frame.

Everything should render exactly as before. If a nametag, sign or compass in an item frame looks wrong, please report it with a screenshot.

Known issues:
- Ionium doesn't show up in Forge's mod list yet. Check F3, it says "Ionium Renderer" on the right.
- The game once hung while saving on exit. We haven't been able to reproduce it since.

Based on Celeritas by embeddedt (LGPL-3.0). Not affiliated with CaffeineMC or the Celeritas project, so please report problems here.
